# Does GaMS refuse like its Qwen teacher? ALT-5 teacher-inheritance screen (iter 2, experiment 7)

This is an exploratory screen under CONFIRM-SPEC v2 of the GaMS3-vs-Gemma-3 bilingual refusal study. All items are
non-reserved DEV-type items. No FINAL or reserved item was touched, and no confirmatory claim is made.

**Question.** GaMS3-12B-Instruct was SFT-ed (among other data) on *GaMS-Nemotron-Chat*, whose responses were generated by
**Qwen3-235B-A22B**. The EN rows are verbatim teacher text; the SL rows are GaMS-27B translations of it. We ask three
things:
* Does GaMS make the same refuse/comply decisions as that teacher?
* Does it word its refusals like the teacher?
* Does that resemblance weaken in Slovene?

Five systems answer byte-identical prompts. Every system uses greedy decoding, an empty system turn and 160 new tokens.

| key | system | role | how run |
|---|---|---|---|
| gams | cjvt/GaMS3-12B-Instruct @1d0b27af | system under test | local, bitsandbytes NF4 (reduced precision) |
| gemma | google/gemma-3-12b-it @96b6f1ec | shared-base sibling (baseline) | local NF4 |
| q14 | Qwen/Qwen3-14B @40c06982 | same-family positive control (FP-cal) | local NF4, `enable_thinking=False` |
| q235 | qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b (original hybrid release) | the SFT data generator (teacher) | OpenRouter, Alibaba pinned, reasoning off (0 reasoning tokens verified), T=0 |
| out | meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct | unrelated outgroup / placebo | OpenRouter, Novita pinned, T=0 |

## Status: what ran, what did not, and the one consequential deviation

* **Done as pre-registered:**
  * the item build (H = 616 HARD-DEV, R = 400 SCORE-400, R200, ID = 117; reserved-id asserts pass);
  * NLLB back-translation;
  * the protocol freeze (`results/protocol.json`, sha256 in `results/protocol_sha256.txt`, git commit `6f07794`, 21:18 UTC,
    before the full pass);
  * the full local generation (3 × 4,082 rows, including the T4 prefill on R200 and the batch-1 checks);
  * the API pilot with its post-freeze checks (`results/pilot_checks_api.json`).
* **Blocker (needs human action).** At 00:33 UTC the **run-level** AI-Inventor OpenRouter budget ran out
  (HTTP 403 `aii_run_budget_exhausted`; "the user can raise the Test idea budget in Configure and resume"). That budget
  is $7.00 for the whole run's "Test idea" phase and is shared by all of the run's artifacts. This artifact's own ledgers
  total **$1.16** of its $10 allowance. Earlier (20:42–00:01 UTC) the shared key had also been at its $50/day limit. The
  state at the stop:
  * **Teacher generation** is complete for H EN/SL, R EN/SL, ID and the 100 retest items. Its EN back-translation arm is
    only partial (72 H + 60 R items); 14 rows were blocked by provider moderation.
  * **Outgroup generation** covers a sha1-random ~80% of H EN/SL and ID, and none of R.
  * **gemini-2.5-flash**, the pre-registered judge, labelled the three LOCAL systems on H EN and SL (616 × 6 cells) plus a
    random part of R. It labelled none of the teacher or outgroup full-pass rows.
  * **Never ran:** the gpt-4.1 second-family judge, the ID judge, and the optional T4-api prefill.

  Neither the teacher nor the outgroup has a `:free` endpoint.
* **Resumed session (Sep 24, 02:58–04:30 UTC).** A platform note said the shared key worked again, so the key was re-probed
  (`results/key_reprobe.json`). The run-level cap still returned 403 `aii_run_budget_exhausted`. The org-wide free-model
  daily limit (1,000/day) was also exhausted until 00:00 UTC on Sep 25. **No paid or free API call succeeded, and spend is unchanged.**
  The session did the following at $0:
  * exported 53 generated-but-unexported API rows (40 teacher, 13 outgroup) and judged them locally;
  * completed the xent scoring;
  * tried and rejected a prefill judge variant (below);
  * re-ran analysis → audit → figures → method_out → report on the final label set. The audit gives 52/52; the headline
    numbers below are from this re-run.
* **Substitute readout (post-freeze deviation).** Judging the teacher with a different instrument than the other systems
  would create a readout-by-system confound, so ONE local judge now scores ALL rows of ALL five systems.
  * Judge: `mistralai/Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501` in NF4, with an explicit empty system turn. It comes from none of
    the five systems' families and uses the SAME frozen P1 / ID prompt text (`src/local_judge.py`).
  * Decision rule: constrained first-token argmax over REFUSE / PARTIAL / COMPLY. The top-1 token was a label in
    14,776/14,776 rows.
  * The plan had said not to use a local judge because iter-1's local judge reached kappa .39, so this judge was
    **validated against gemini** before use. Binary REFUSE kappa by cell:
    * H k0, local systems: 0.67–0.86, with n = 616 per cell (pooled 0.75);
    * teacher pilot cells: 0.74 (EN) and 0.82 (SL), n = 32 each;
    * outgroup pilot cells: 0.30 (EN) and 0.87 (SL), n = 32 each. The weak EN outgroup cell limits T1b.
  * Known weaknesses:
    * It calls REFUSE more often than gemini (0.43 vs 0.38 on H).
    * Its PARTIAL boundary is unreliable (PARTIAL-as-refusal kappa ≈ 0.46), so the PARTIAL-recode robustness rows are
      weak.
    * It is **not valid on prefill rows** (pooled kappa 0.15, n = 151). It labels real compliance after "Sure, here is
      a…" as REFUSE, so the T4 depth verdict under this readout is UNINTERPRETABLE.
  * A post-hoc prefill-specific prompt for the same judge (`--variant prefill_v2`) was tried in the resumed session and
    **rejected** (`results/prefill_v2_validation.json`). Its pre-declared held-out gate passed numerically (kappa 0.79, n = 101)
    but was degenerate: the held-out rows exclude every row on which the old prompt disagreed with gemini, and the old prompt
    scores 1.00 on them. On the 33 disagreement rows the variant matches gemini on 7. A blind 50-row adjudication by the
    executing agent (Claude, **not a human**; `labels/prefill_adjudication_agent.json`) agrees with gemini on 42/50, the old
    prompt on 21/50 and the variant on 25/50. So on prefill rows gemini is the credible readout, and the local judge stays invalid.
  * Two more readouts are kept: the gemini readout on its partial coverage (`results/analysis_gemini_partial.json`) and a
    lexical readout (`results/analysis_regex.json`).

## Results (substitute readout unless stated; every number is in `results/analysis.json`, audit 52/52 re-derivations agree)

1. **Decision inheritance (T1) is not detected, and the pre-registered instrument fails its own calibration.**
   * **FP-cal, HARD-DEV EN:** kappa(Q14,Q235) − kappa(Q14,Gemma) = **−0.001 [−0.074, 0.079]** (n = 608). Even a
     same-family model that was distilled from the flagship does not agree more with it than with Gemma on over-refusal
     decisions. Per the pre-registration, T1 is therefore **UNINTERPRETABLE**.
   * **Point estimates, descriptive:**
     * dk = kappa(GaMS,Q235) − kappa(GaMS,Gemma) = **−0.044 [−0.118, 0.032]**. The 90% CI is [−0.107, 0.021], so a
       teacher advantage of ≥ 0.10 kappa is excluded. Formal ±0.10 equivalence narrowly fails on the lower side.
     * T1b (vs Llama) = 0.062 [−0.024, 0.151], n = 487.
     * Side-taking on the 117 items where Q235 ≠ Gemma: GaMS sides with Q235 as often as the Llama placebo does
       (difference −0.009 [−0.133, 0.123]).
     * Fingerprint partial r after difficulty controls: Q235 0.27, Gemma 0.27, Llama 0.01.
   * **Pairwise kappas:** all 10 are 0.48–0.60. Decision agreement on these items is dominated by shared item
     difficulty, not by lineage.
   * **Robustness:** the lexical readout gives the same null (dk 0.075 [−0.020, 0.177]; FP-cal −0.129). The local-system
     kappa structure matches gemini's (gemini H EN: GaMS~Gemma .64, GaMS~Q14 .66, Gemma~Q14 .65; substitute .59, .59,
     .54).
2. **Language (T2).** On Slovene prompts Gemma over-refuses (safe-item refusal 0.52 SL vs 0.27 EN), whereas GaMS
   (−0.06), the teacher (−0.19), Q14 and Llama all refuse *less* in SL than in EN.
   * The SL "resemblance" follows from this: dk(SL) = 0.082 [−0.004, 0.162] and FP-cal(SL) = 0.19 [0.11, 0.27].
     Both are driven by Gemma being the outlier; T1b(SL) = 0.002.
   * DiffGap dk(EN) − dk(SL) = **−0.133 [−0.247, −0.011]**, which is the opposite sign to the ALT-5 prediction.
   * The EN-BT language contrast has n = 70 and is estimate-only (0.005 [−0.293, 0.327]).
   * GaMS's SFT removed Gemma's Slovene over-refusal. This matches every non-Gemma model and is not teacher-specific.
3. **Wording (T3): strong, and it follows the SFT DATA rather than the live teacher.**
   * **EN:**
     * 76.1% [73.7, 78.4] of GaMS refusal first sentences occur verbatim among its SFT refusal first sentences
       (teacher 75.7%, Gemma 0.0%, Llama 25%).
     * A char 2–5-gram source classifier (Sun et al. 2025; CV accuracy 0.97) labels **95.8%** of GaMS EN refusals as
       teacher-like (positive control Q14 96.7%; the SFT texts themselves 95.7%).
     * Opening-trigram JSD GaMS~Q235 0.53 vs GaMS~Gemma 1.00.
   * **SL:** GaMS says "Oprostite, vendar vam …" (89% of its SL refusals). This is the GaMS-27B translation found in its
     SFT data: 90.8% of GaMS's SL first sentences are verbatim in the translated SFT refusals, but only 1.5% of the
     teacher's native-Slovene first sentences are ("Na žalost ne …"). The SL classifier therefore assigns GaMS mostly to
     *Llama* (79%): none of the live systems carries the translated wording.
   * **Beyond refusals:** GaMS's compliant answers to safe items are also teacher-like (classifier share 0.90, CV 0.90).
   * **Exploratory white-box likelihood (xent, post-freeze):** GaMS rates the teacher's EN text as relatively more likely
     than Gemma does (+0.15 [0.09, 0.21] nats/char). This comes from compliant answers (+0.09); refusal texts show none
     (−0.01, n = 164) because every model finds "I'm sorry, but I can't…" probable.
   * The pre-registered SL formula regex is **not discriminative**: Gemma's "Žal mi je, vendar" matches the Qwen-SL
     pattern.
4. **Depth (T4): inconclusive.** The substitute judge is invalid on prefill rows. The primary gemini judge on its
   labelled random subset (n ≈ 24 per bar) gives these compliant-prefix non-refusal rates:
   * EN: GaMS 0.33 [0.18, 0.53], Gemma 0.13 [0.05, 0.32], Q14 0.44 [0.26, 0.63];
   * SL: GaMS 0.04, Gemma 0.07, Q14 0.19;
   * neutral prefix: ≈ 0 everywhere.

   No depth claim is made; the optional T4-api prefill was not run.
5. **Identity (T5, descriptive).** GaMS mentions Qwen/Alibaba in 47% [35, 60] of EN identity answers but only 7% of SL
   ones (Gemma 0%; Q235 97%; Q14 98%). It self-names "Qwen" in 21% of EN ID answers. The chrF of GaMS's identity answers
   is higher to the teacher's answer than to Gemma's (EN 33.1 vs 25.5, Wilcoxon p = 2e-5). This again points to
   inheritance of EN text, with the SL identity corrections from the SFT translation step visible as well.
6. **Validity.**
   * Teacher test-retest kappa is 0.88 (only 17% of texts are identical at T=0: the provider is non-deterministic).
   * Language consistency is ≥ 0.98 on every H arm.
   * Labels at 64 vs 160 tokens agree at 0.97–1.00 with iter 1.
   * Batch-vs-single binary outcomes agree: GaMS 32/32, Q14 15/16, Gemma 13/16 (Gemma's disagreements sit at the
     PARTIAL boundary with near-identical text).
   * The placebo label swap centres at 0.

**Bottom line for the paper.**
* GaMS inherited its teacher's *wording*: the EN surface form verbatim, and the SL form via the translator.
* This screen finds no evidence that it inherited the teacher's *refuse/comply decisions*.
* Kappa agreement on over-refusal items cannot even detect Qwen3-14B's resemblance to its own flagship, so the decision
  test lacks the resolution to show inheritance. The negative result is therefore one of **instrument insensitivity plus
  an excluded large effect (dk < 0.10)**, not proof of absence.
* The teacher-decision numbers rest on a validated substitute judge. Re-running `./finalize.sh` after the budget is
  raised adds the pre-registered gemini/gpt-4.1 readout (it is resumable).

## Provenance facts verified against primary sources

* **`cjvt/GaMS-Nemotron-Chat` card:** the responses come from *Qwen3 235B A22B* (via NVIDIA Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset-v1).
  They were translated to Slovene by GaMS-27B-Instruct (80:20 SL:EN).
* **`cjvt/GaMS3-12B-Instruct@1d0b27af` card:** the chat and safety SFT used **Nemotron-Chat** (88,126 train rows) **plus
  GaMS-Safety** (459 Slovene safety items, not from Qwen). Qwen text is therefore only one source of GaMS's refusal
  behaviour. Excerpts are in `data/provenance_model_cards.txt`.
* **OpenRouter:** the original hybrid `qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b` is served only by Alibaba (quantisation undisclosed); see
  `logs/openrouter_endpoints.json`. Both providers are recorded per row.

## Layout

| path | content |
|---|---|
| `method.py` | single entry point: runs the stage scripts in order (`--stage all\|items\|bt\|gpu\|api\|judge\|xent\|analyze\|report`) |
| `src/common.py` | constants: systems and pinned revisions, seed 20260924, prefixes, paths, priority tiers |
| `src/build_items.py` | STEP 0: `data/items.jsonl` (H, R, R200, ID), `data/ref_sft.jsonl` (3,057 GaMS SFT refusal texts); reserved-id asserts |
| `src/gpu_gen.py` | NLLB back-translation (`data/h_en_bt.jsonl`); NF4 generation, T4 prefill, batch-vs-single |
| `src/api_gen.py`, `src/orclient.py` | teacher/outgroup generation (+ optional prefill); resumable cost-capped ledger, provider pin, outage pause, budget stop |
| `src/judge.py` | pre-registered gemini readout, gpt-4.1 second family, ID judge, 403 fallback |
| `src/local_judge.py`, `src/judge_agreement.py` | SUBSTITUTE judge (Mistral-Small-24B NF4) and its agreement with gemini per cell |
| `src/rederive_headline.py` | independent re-derivation of headline numbers + placebos -> `results/rederive_headline.json` |
| `reproducibility.md` | exact commands, versions, hardware and expected numbers |
| `src/prefill_v2_validation.py` | post-hoc prefill judge variant check -> `results/prefill_v2_validation.json` (REJECTED) |
| `src/freeze.py` | writes and hashes `results/protocol.json` |
| `src/analyze.py`, `src/stats.py` | FP-cal, T1 (dk, T1b, fingerprint, joint logit, side-taking, strata, placebo, retest), T2, T3, T4, T5, validity, verdicts; `--readout local\|gemini\|regex` |
| `src/xent.py` | EXPLORATORY white-box likelihood of teacher vs outgroup texts under GaMS / Gemma / Q14 |
| `src/audit.py` | independent plain-python recomputation -> `results/audit.json` |
| `src/make_figs.py`, `src/make_report.py`, `src/make_method_out.py` | figures, `results/RESULTS.md`, `method_out.json` |
| `src/pilot_checks.py`, `src/wait_key.py` | pilot confirmation signals; key poller |
| `tests/test_pipeline.py` | unit tests (kappa vs sklearn, bootstrap, JSD) + synthetic end-to-end run of both readouts |
| `data/` | items, back-translations, prefix strings, SFT refusal references, model-card excerpts, items manifest (sha256) |
| `gens/` | per-item generations `{system}.jsonl` (key = item_id\|system\|lang_arm\|condition), API ledgers, `xent_*.jsonl`, `pilot/` (never pooled) |
| `labels/` | `refusal_gemini.jsonl` (primary, partial), `refusal_local.jsonl` + `idname_local.jsonl` (substitute), ledgers, `pilot/` (validation), `refusal_local_prefill_v2.jsonl` (rejected variant), `prefill_adjudication_agent.json` (agent, not human) |
| `results/` | `protocol.json` (+sha256), `analysis.json` (substitute, headline), `analysis_gemini_partial.json`, `analysis_regex.json`, `audit.json`, `RESULTS.md`, pilot checks, key probes, throughput |
| `figures/` | fig1 kappa matrices, fig2 dk forest, fig3 opening trigrams, fig4 prefill flips (gemini subset), fig5 identity names (png+pdf) |
| `method_out.json` (+ full_/mini_/preview_) | exp_gen_sol_out: one example per item × arm × condition; `output` = teacher label, `predict_<system>` = substitute label; gemini labels as metadata |
| `run_gpu_chain.sh`, `finalize.sh`, `run_local_judge.sh`, `run_when_key_resets.sh` | one-command reruns |

All outputs stay at this workspace path:
`.`.

## How to run

```bash
uv sync                                   # pinned deps (pyproject.toml / uv.lock; torch 2.14, transformers 4.57.6, bitsandbytes)
.venv/bin/python method.py --stage items && .venv/bin/python method.py --stage bt
./run_gpu_chain.sh                        # GaMS -> Gemma -> Qwen3-14B NF4 generation (resumable, ~1.3 GPU-h on an RTX 4090)
./finalize.sh                             # API generation -> gemini/gpt-4.1 judging -> xent -> analysis (needs OpenRouter budget)
./run_local_judge.sh                      # $0 substitute readout + prefill_v2 variant (~45 min GPU), then:
cd src && ../.venv/bin/python analyze.py --readout local && ../.venv/bin/python analyze.py --readout gemini \
  && ../.venv/bin/python analyze.py --readout regex && ../.venv/bin/python prefill_v2_validation.py && ../.venv/bin/python audit.py && ../.venv/bin/python make_figs.py \
  && ../.venv/bin/python make_method_out.py && ../.venv/bin/python make_report.py
AII_TEST_ROOT=/tmp/x .venv/bin/python tests/test_pipeline.py   # synthetic tests (never touch real outputs)
```
The script needs `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL`. Requests must go to the base URL (a proxy) and carry a
browser-like User-Agent. Paid calls stop at a cumulative $9 over all ledgers.

## Restoring removed files

Only regenerable or redownloadable bulk is marked `delete` in `.aii/manifest.yaml`:

* **`.venv/`:** `uv sync` (pinned in `pyproject.toml` / `uv.lock`).
* **`src/__pycache__/`:** regenerated on import.
* **Model weights** live in the run's SHARED HF cache (`$HF_HOME`), not in this directory. To restore them:
  * `huggingface-cli download cjvt/GaMS3-12B-Instruct --revision 1d0b27af5748784482600d24779409e7e1dc9adc`
  * `huggingface-cli download google/gemma-3-12b-it --revision 96b6f1eccf38110c56df3a15bffe176da04bfd80`
  * `huggingface-cli download Qwen/Qwen3-14B --revision 40c069824f4251a91eefaf281ebe4c544efd3e18`
  * `huggingface-cli download facebook/nllb-200-distilled-1.3B`
  * `huggingface-cli download mistralai/Mistral-Small-24B-Instruct-2501 --revision 9527884be6e5616bdd54de542f9ae13384489724 --include "model-*.safetensors" "*.json" "tokenizer*"`
